title: MAGE-A4/MAGE-A8-targeted TCR-based bispecific T cell engager in recurrent and/or refractory solid tumors: a phase 1 trial
one_line: Phase 1 first-in-human basket trial of IMA401, a half-life-extended TCR-based bispecific engager (TCER) against an HLA-A*02:01-presented MAGE-A4/MAGE-A8 peptide with a deliberately low-affinity CD3 arm, in 61 heavily pretreated solid tumor patients.
key_claims: MTD was not reached per protocol across a 0.0066–2.5 mg dose range; RP2D was set at 1–2 mg biweekly, enabled by a silenced Fc giving ~15.4–17.5 day half-life.
Confirmed ORR was 14% (8/56) in the overall efficacy-evaluable population including subtherapeutic starting doses, and 20% (8/41) at RP2D across 15 indications (post hoc).
In the largest RP2D subgroup, head and neck cancer, ORR was 29% (4/14) with 64% disease control and median duration of response 8.8 months; one melanoma patient had ongoing PFS >33.9 months.

Safety: TRAEs in 89% of patients, CRS 38% (grades 1–2 only), transient lymphopenia 33%, neutropenia 31%, zero ICANS; 3/7 patients at 2.5 mg had DLT grade 4 neutropenia, and no further DLTs occurred in the RP2D range after 8 mg dexamethasone premedication plus step dosing.
Pembrolizumab combination showed no additive toxicity versus monotherapy, with objective responses including patients who had progressed on prior checkpoint inhibitors.
limitations: Single-arm phase 1 prespecified interim analysis with no comparator; RP2D-specific ORR was a post hoc analysis.
Small and highly heterogeneous subgroups (e.g., 14 head and neck patients, 7 patients at 2.5 mg) limit precision of response and toxicity estimates.
Therapy is restricted to HLA-A*02:01-positive, MAGE-A4/A8-expressing patients, narrowing generalizability.
One possibly treatment-related death (pneumonia with neutropenia) occurred at 2.5 mg without dexamethasone premedication and was confounded by rapidly progressing lung metastases.
Mechanistic claims about the low-affinity CD3 arm avoiding peripheral T-cell sink and exhaustion are design rationale, not directly demonstrated clinical endpoints in the reported data.
open_questions: Does a randomized trial at the 1–2 mg RP2D, particularly in head and neck cancer, confirm the response rate and show survival benefit?
Is the pembrolizumab combination additive over IMA401 monotherapy in checkpoint-refractory patients, or are responses attributable to IMA401 alone?
Do pharmacodynamic data confirm reduced peripheral T-cell sequestration and better tumor penetration versus a high-affinity CD3 comparator?
What drives escape in non-responders — HLA loss, antigen downregulation, or T-cell exhaustion within the tumor?
Can the same TCER architecture against other intracellular antigens (e.g., PRAME with IMA402) and other HLA alleles reproduce this safety and efficacy profile?
